tasks.title: Refactor NeoMud Three toward bird eye click to move play
tasks.description: Explore and implement a click-first play mode for NeoMud Three: Diablo 3-inspired elevated camera, click-to-move, clickable world landmarks/exits/interactables, readable loot/NPC affordances, room-to-room action-RPG flow, and reduced reliance on camera-facing sign labels that can clip into geometry. comments.body: User clarified target feel: StarCraft II / Dota-like camera and interaction, not first-person or third-person chase. Refined target: Diablo-like is probably the better fit for NeoMud Three than RTS/MOBA. Single-character click-to-move, elevated readable camera, click NPCs/items/exits, room graph remains server-authoritative.

Product direction clarified: ship a game obviously heavily inspired by Diablo 3 mechanics. Prioritize elevated/isometric camera, click-to-move, click attacks/interactions/exits, readable loot/NPC affordances, room-to-room flow, and action-RPG pacing. Preserve NeoMud server authority and MUD room graph under the presentation layer.

First visual-mode slice implemented: HUD camera toggle supports Platform and Iso. Platform preserves the current behind-character pointer-lock view; Iso provides elevated ARPG camera and keeps cursor visible for future click-to-move. Next slice should add ground raycast click target, destination marker, and clickable exits through the existing move command path.

First click-to-move slice implemented: Iso mode canvas clicks raycast to the ground plane, clamp through room runtime, show a destination marker, and steer the avatar toward the target. Keyboard movement cancels the click target. QA includes debug API movement plus real browser mouse click in Town Square Iso screenshot test. Remaining gap: direct click selection for exits/NPCs/items.

Direct click routing added: ground clicks now check nearby interactables and exit trigger volumes before defaulting to movement. Town Square QA verifies Old Wren click selection opens the interaction panel and North Gate trigger click routes to town:gate through the existing move path. Remaining gap: hover/selection feedback and pathing.

First hover targeting slice implemented: Iso mode classifies pointer/ground targets, shows a world hover marker plus concise Click prompt for NPCs/items/exits, and clears hover on click, room switch, player placement, pointer leave, or panel state. Town Square screenshot QA now verifies Old Wren hover and North Gate hover before existing click routing.

Selection affordance slice added: clicking an interactable in Iso mode now leaves a selected-target world ring while the interaction panel is open, and body cursor state changes on hoverable NPC/item/exit targets. Town Square screenshot QA now captures isometric-selection-target and budget remains within the 240-call gate.

Target prompt semantics tightened: hover/proximity labels now use entity prompt/action data so normal NPCs read Talk to, hostiles read Engage, objects read Inspect, and loot reads Pick up. Offline smoke QA now asserts Forest Rat and Shadow Wolf hover/proximity labels read as Engage.

Selection lifetime tightened: selected-target ring is now scoped to the interaction panel and clears on Escape/close or when opening a non-interaction panel. Town Square screenshot QA asserts the marker clears after closing Old Wren.

Object-level target response added: hover and selected interactables now pulse the actual scene group when a user targets them in Iso mode, with selection overriding hover. Town Square QA asserts Old Wren object highlighting for hover and selection.

Click-to-interact now uses an approach flow: clicking an interactable selects/highlights it, routes the avatar to an approach point, tracks a pendingInteraction in debug state, and opens the panel only once in range. Town Square QA covers Old Wren real-click and debug-click approach behavior.

Live hostile Basic Attack is now wired through the Kotlin protocol instead of remaining a disabled placeholder: the client sends select_target plus attack_toggle for the selected hostile, tracks attack_mode_update/combat_hit/npc_died responses, and exposes combat state in the debug API. Server-backed QA verifies Giant Forest Spider can be selected and attack mode enabled.

Combat UI now has a reversible engaged state: after attack_mode_update confirms the selected hostile is active, the action row switches Basic Attack to Stop Attack, shows an Attacking pill, and sends attack_toggle(false) to disengage. Server-backed QA verifies both attack-on and stop-attack paths.

Hostile target health is now live-state capable: combat_hit messages cache defender HP/max HP by hostile id, npc_died drops the target to 0 HP, and the target frame renders the live server values instead of only deterministic placeholder health. Offline smoke QA injects a combat_hit for Giant Forest Spider and verifies the panel updates to 18/32.

Combat hit feedback now appears in the 3D world: combat_hit creates a short-lived floating damage/miss/dodge/parry sprite at the defender position, npc_died can emit Defeated feedback, and debug effects exposes a combat count. Offline smoke QA verifies the injected Giant Forest Spider combat_hit creates a combat effect.

Selected hostile targets now show an in-world HP bar attached to the selected-target ring. The bar mirrors live targetHealthById values from combat_hit/npc_died and exposes healthBarVisible/value/ratio through debug selection state. Offline smoke QA verifies Giant Forest Spider shows 18/32 and the expected ratio after an injected combat_hit.

Iso click-and-hold movement added: primary pointer down on open ground starts hold movement, pointer drag updates the destination marker continuously, and pointer release stops hold state while preserving the active destination. Town Square screenshot QA uses a real mouse drag and captures isometric-hold-move.

Iso camera zoom added: mouse wheel in Iso mode adjusts a bounded zoom multiplier used by the render-engine isometric camera. Debug API exposes cameraControls, and Town Square screenshot QA verifies wheel-down zooms out and wheel-up zooms back in.

First hostile target affordance slice added: hostile interactables use red selected-target marker colors and the interaction panel renders a compact hostile target frame with deterministic health bar. Smoke QA verifies Giant Forest Spider opens the hostile target frame. This is target UI only, not a local combat simulation.

Hostile action row added: hostile interaction panels now show disabled Basic Attack and class-skill slots with explicit server-authoritative combat command messaging. Smoke QA asserts the action row, two disabled command slots, and screenshot evidence in offline-hostile-target-panel.png.

Iso right-click cancel added: right-click on the canvas clears click movement, hover, selection, and panels without opening the browser context menu. Town Square screenshot QA verifies state clears after hold-move.

Feature action wording corrected: treasure/drop features now read Open rather than Pick up, disabled action buttons preserve their verb such as Open unavailable, and smoke QA verifies Hidden Cave chest hover/proximity/action-button semantics.

Hidden Cave live item loot now carries PICKUP_ITEM action and debug metadata, matching coin-pile pickup affordances. Verified offline smoke, Town Square screenshot QA, and server-backed chest loot/pickup/inventory flow.

Room debug entity serialization consolidated through one helper so action type, item id, coin type, quantity, prompt, and position metadata are exposed consistently across authored rooms. Verified offline smoke, Town Square screenshots, and server-backed QA.

Corrected the click-target collision approach after user QA: do not invalidate ordinary clicks merely because the straight segment crosses a collider. Destination placement now relies on existing room collision pushout so clicks inside the Town Square fountain clamp outside it, while clicks beyond props remain valid until a real navmesh/pathfinding pass exists.

Iso is now the default camera mode, with ?camera=platform preserving the behind-character mode. Real canvas clicks on Iso interactables no longer close the interaction panel through the follow-up click handler. Iso starts slightly zoomed out and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight rotate the Iso camera orbit. Town Square QA covers default zoom, ArrowRight orbit, real-click Old Wren panel persistence, normal click-to-move, and click target behavior around the fountain.
Iso keyboard movement is now screen/camera-relative for WASD and ArrowUp/ArrowDown. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight rotate the Iso camera orbit and do not move the avatar. Town Square QA asserts both behaviors.

Hostile click flow now matches the ARPG direction more closely: clicking a hostile target while connected to the Kotlin server selects/approaches it and automatically starts the server attack loop via select_target plus attack_toggle. Offline mode still only opens the hostile panel rather than faking combat. Server-backed QA verifies clicking Giant Forest Spider sets attackMode and selectedTargetId without pressing the Basic Attack button.

Selected non-hostile interactables now get a small in-world action badge attached to the selected-target ring. The badge is color/shape coded for Open, Talk, item pickup, and coin pickup without adding floating text labels. Offline QA verifies the Hidden Cave chest shows an Open/TREASURE_DROP badge; server-backed QA verifies live Cave Loot shows Pick up with PICKUP_ITEM/PICKUP_COINS semantics.

Selection cleanup hardened: room changes now close any open panel, clear selected interactable/action result state, and force selected health/action badges to hide with empty debug metadata. Offline QA opens the Hidden Cave chest, switches rooms, and verifies the panel, marker, action badge, and selectedInteractableId are cleared.

Server-backed actionable non-hostile clicks now auto-use through the same authoritative command path: clicking the Hidden Cave chest sends interact_feature after selection/approach, and clicking live Cave Loot sends pickup item/coins without requiring a second DOM button click. Offline mode still only opens the panel. Server-backed QA verifies autoUse flags and real server state changes for chest and loot.

Server interact_result messages now create immediate world-space action feedback at the selected object: Opened/Used for success and No effect for failed interactions. The hostile combat command path now uses the same prompt-derived isHostileEntity classifier as targeting, fixing auto-engage brittleness. Server-backed QA verifies chest auto-use produces a world-space effect after the real server response.

Interaction feedback now has its own render-engine queue and debug counter instead of reusing combat effects. Server-backed chest QA now asserts effects.interaction increments on interact_result, while combat damage and pickup sparkle counts remain separate.

Server-backed world actions now track pendingInteractionAction while an interact/pickup command is in flight. Repeat use commands are ignored until interact_result/pickup_result clears the pending state. Debug exposes pendingInteractionAction, and server-backed QA verifies chest and loot auto-use set the pending id and clear it after the server result.

Combat commands now use server-confirmed pending state instead of optimistic attack toggles. pendingCombatCommand suppresses repeat sends, action buttons show Working/Awaiting server while pending, and attackMode/selectedTargetId update from attack_mode_update. Server-backed QA verifies click auto-attack and Stop Attack set pending command state and clear it after server confirmation.

Combat action hotkeys added: Digit1/Numpad1 trigger the primary hostile action, which means Basic Attack when idle and Stop Attack when engaged; Digit2/Numpad2 trigger the class spell/skill slot when available. The hotkeys reuse the same action-option definitions as the rendered buttons and respect pendingCombatCommand. Server-backed QA verifies Digit1 starts and then stops attack through the Kotlin server.

Selected hostile debug state now exposes combatActions metadata: hotkey, label, detail, command, and enabled state. Hotkeys and rendered buttons share the same combatActionOptions source. Offline and server-backed QA assert action metadata for disabled offline combat, idle attack, pending Working state, and engaged Stop Attack.

Iso exit clicks now route through movement before changing rooms: clicking an exit stores pendingExit, shows the normal destination/path preview, walks the avatar to the trigger, and only then dispatches the existing room move. Town Square QA asserts North Gate click creates pendingExit plus a visible movement marker before transitioning. Server-backed QA was hardened for fast chest interact_result responses that can clear pendingInteractionAction before the test samples it.

Hover/selection now applies a bounded temporary material response to the actual target object in addition to scale pulsing and rings. Target mesh/sprite materials are cloned, tinted/emissive-pulsed while highlighted, restored/disposed on clear, and guarded against per-frame recloning. Debug exposes objectHighlightMaterialCount; Town Square QA asserts hover/selection material response and cleanup.

Target persistence rule added: closing an interaction panel now hides the DOM panel but keeps the selected world target/ring/material response active until explicit cancel, room change, or a non-interaction panel clears it. Town Square QA verifies Old Wren remains selected after panel close and clears through cancelIsoTargeting.

Physical Town Square exit boards now carry exitAffordance metadata and are directly clickable in Iso mode. The renderer exposes raycastable world targets, pointer hover/click checks those before falling back to ground-plane movement, and clicking the Gate board routes through the same pendingExit/startPendingExit path as trigger-volume clicks. Town Square QA clicks the Gate board and verifies either pending NORTH exit travel or fast transition to town:gate.

Shared authored-room exit gateway labels now use fixed mesh boards with exitAffordance metadata, so non-Town-Square gateways can be clicked directly in Iso mode. Text-board debug positions are world-space for grouped gateway labels. Room-shot QA clicks the Forest Edge -> Forest Path gateway board and verifies NORTH pending-exit travel or fast transition to forest:path.

Authored interactable fixtures can now opt into physical object clicking with interactableAffordance metadata. The Hidden Cave moss-covered chest carries cave_chest metadata on its visible mesh group; Iso raycasting resolves that to the existing server-authoritative interaction approach path. Offline smoke QA clicks the authored chest mesh directly and verifies cave_chest selection/pending interaction before the existing proximity panel checks.
